title: Why Dogs Sniff Each Other's Butts
topic: Why do dogs sniff each other's butts?

beats.label: rear-end greeting
lines: Dogs treat another dog's rear end like a social profile.

beats.label: more sensitive than humans
lines: Their sense of smell is forty times more sensitive than ours.
Each odor contains volatile molecules that differ in concentration and volatility.
Dogs detect them with an extraordinary sense of smell.

beats.title: Why the rear?
lines: Dogs mark territory with urine and stools.
A rear sniff samples pheromones from urine and an anal-gland signature from feces, identifying the marker and the place.

beats.title: Scent signals
lines: Those scents can signal sex and age, plus female estrus, pregnancy, or recent birth.
Different hormones are also released when a dog feels angry, fearful, or confident.
Next time two dogs meet, watch their greeting.
That rear sniff is a quick scent-based identity check.

sources.claim: Dogs' sense of smell is forty times more sensitive than a human's, and scents and pheromones are used for communication.
Urine contains pheromone chemicals, canine anal glands give fecal deposits a signature identifying the marker and location, and scent signatures can indicate sex, age, and reproductive status.
Different hormones are secreted when a dog is angry, fearful, or confident.
Individual odors consist of volatile organic molecules that differ in magnitude, volatility, and concentration, and canines have an extraordinary olfactory sense.
